users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Manage your department’s staff: who can sign in, and what they may do.

dialog.addDescription: Each role only sees the modules and pages its work needs.
dialog.selfNote: You cannot change your own role or status.
dialog.activeDescription: Deactivated users cannot sign in, and existing sessions stop working immediately.
dialog.lockedNotice: Locked out after too many failed sign-ins.
dialog.defaultPasswordNote: The account starts on the {role} default password. The user has to replace it on their first sign-in.
dialog.noRoleDefault: The {role} role has no default password yet.
dialog.noRoleDefaultLink: Set it at the bottom of this page

sessions.title: Signed-in devices — {name}
sessions.description: Where this account is signed in now, and the last few sessions that ended.
sessions.endAllHint: {name} will be signed out on every device and has to sign in again.
sessions.ended: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to sign out} one {Signed out # session of {name}} other {Signed out # sessions of {name}}}.

users.mustChangeHint: This account is still on a password from an administrator (the role default) and will be asked to replace it at the next sign-in.

resetDefault.title: Reset to default password
resetDefault.confirm: {name}'s password goes back to the {role} default. Every device they are signed in on is signed out, and they must replace the password on their next sign-in.
resetDefault.done: {name}'s password was reset to the default.

users.adminsSubtitle: Manage the admin account of each department. Each admin manages their own features and staff.

signInAudit.title: Sign-in Audit
signInAudit.subtitle: Who signed in, and what they proved besides a password.
signInAudit.summaryHint: Counted across every matching row, not just this page. Picking a result filters the list below; this row still shows all of them.
signInAudit.summaryEmpty: No sign-in attempts match these filters.

admin.title: Administration
admin.subtitle: Announcements above every page, and a full backup of every module’s data.

rolePasswords.title: Default password per role
rolePasswords.description: Every new account starts on its role's default, and a forgotten password is reset to it. The person then has to replace it on their next sign-in.
rolePasswords.notSetHint: Accounts of this role cannot be created or reset yet.
rolePasswords.note: Stored encrypted and never shown again. A change applies to new accounts and later resets only; accounts already on the old default keep it.
rolePasswords.dialogDescription: Write it down somewhere safe to pass on to new users: it cannot be shown again after saving.
rolePasswords.tooShort: The password must be at least 8 characters.

announcements.title: Announcements
announcements.description: A banner above every page, for everybody or for some roles. Info can be closed by each reader; a warning stays up until it ends.
announcements.messagePlaceholder: e.g. XRF maintenance tomorrow 08:00–10:00. Hold analysis samples until then.
announcements.rolesHint: Tick none to show it to everybody.
announcements.timesHint: Leave the start empty to show it now, and the end empty to keep it until you end it.

backup.title: Backup
backup.description: Everything in one Excel workbook: every sample with its results (deleted ones included and marked), the stage log, result changes, master data, stages and users.
backup.excluded: Not included: passwords, authenticator secrets, face readings and sign-in sessions. Keep the file somewhere safe; it holds every result.

users.title: Users
users.intro: The Super Admin manages each department’s admin accounts; the Lab Admin manages the lab staff.

steps.1: Add a user with a role (and a department, for the Super Admin); Edit changes the role, resets the password, unlocks or deactivates.
steps.2: From the ⋯ menu: enrol a face, require an authenticator app, or see the devices signed in.
steps.3: Each role’s default password is set at the bottom of this page.

users.tip: Resetting a password signs that person out on every device, so use it when a password may be known to someone else.

admin.title: Administration
admin.intro: Announcements above every page, the sign-in audit, and the full backup.

steps.1: Write an announcement, choose Info or Warning and who sees it; set start and end, or leave them empty.
steps.2: End now takes it down but keeps it in the list; Delete removes it.
steps.3: Sign-in Audit shows who signed in, from where, and who was refused, across every department.
steps.4: Download backup gives one Excel file with all the data, without passwords or secrets.

1.title: You look after the admins
1.body: Admin Accounts is where each department’s admin is created and managed: Lab and Exploration. Each admin runs their own module.

2.title: System settings
2.body: Administration posts announcements and downloads backups; Sign-in Audit shows who signed in.

3.title: Help is always here
3.body: Press ? at the top of any page for the part of the guide about it.

2.title: Add a user
2.body: Create an account with its role. Saved when you press Save in the form.

3.title: Verification
3.body: Shows whether a face or an authenticator app is active for the account.

4.title: Edit
4.body: Change the role, reset the password, unlock or deactivate.

5.title: More
5.body: Enrol a face, manage the authenticator, or see the devices signed in.

1.title: Write an announcement
1.body: A short message shown above every page.

2.title: Type and audience
2.body: Info can be closed by readers; a Warning stays up. Tick roles, or none for everybody.

3.title: Schedule
3.body: Set when it starts and ends (WITA), or leave them empty.

4.title: Publish
4.body: The announcement shows to its audience straight away.

5.title: Backup
5.body: Download all the data as one Excel file, without passwords or secrets.
